title: Group and operation
parts: The group with underlying set G and operation ∗.
example: In (ℤ,+), the set is the integers and the operation is addition.
note: The operation ∗ may be addition or composition.
wrong: G is the group identity and ∗ is always multiplication.
G is the number of elements in the group.

title: Group identity
parts: Combining e with g in either order
example: In the additive group of integers, e = 0.
note: The identity depends on the operation. The additive identity is 0.
wrong: e is an inverse for each g.

title: Group inverse
example: In (ℤ,+), the inverse of 5 is −5 because 5 + (−5) = 0.
note: The superscript −1 refers to the group operation.
wrong: The inverse of g is always the reciprocal 1/g.
Combining g with itself gives e in every group.

title: Subgroup
parts: H is a subgroup of G.
example: The even integers under addition form a subgroup of the integers under addition.
note: A subset must itself be a group under the same operation.
wrong: H is a real number at most G.
Every subset H is a subgroup.

title: Normal subgroup
parts: N is a normal subgroup of G.
example: The even integers form a normal subgroup of the additive integers, since the group is abelian.
note: Normality means gNg⁻¹ = N for each g in G.
wrong: N is any subset of G with fewer elements.
N is the inverse of G.

title: Left coset
parts: The set of all products gh with h in the subgroup H.
example: In additive ℤ, 1 + 2ℤ is the coset of all odd integers.
note: A coset need not contain the identity.
wrong: The subgroup containing only the element g.
The result of multiplying g by the size of H.

title: Quotient group
parts: The group whose elements are cosets of the normal subgroup N.
example: ℤ/2ℤ has two cosets, even and odd, with addition modulo 2.
note: Normality makes the coset operation well defined.
wrong: The set remaining after deleting N from G.
The ratio of the sizes of the sets, treated as a group element.

title: Group homomorphism
parts: Applying φ to a product gives the product of the images.
example: The map φ(n) = 2n on additive integers satisfies φ(a+b) = φ(a)+φ(b).
note: A homomorphism preserves the operation. It need not be one-to-one.
wrong: φ must map every element to itself.

title: Polynomial ring
parts: The ring of polynomials in x with coefficients in R.
note: Elements have finitely many terms and non-negative integer exponents.
wrong: The value of the function R at input x.
All rational functions with coefficients in R.
